answer: Each agent periodically emits a signed signal tied to a unique cryptographic key recorded in the system’s atlas. The network assigns a quadratic weight to an identity’s reputation: one ferrous‑strength node contributes weight 1, while n freshly minted IDs together contribute only √n, so spawning thousands of fake profiles yields diminishing influence. An attacker must therefore invest proportional to the square of the desired impact, making large Sybil assaults economically prohibitive.
